utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I will address the witness, Mr. Antic. You have to take the oath again, the solemn declaration, rather. Will you please stand up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. The last time you were here, the Trial Chamber informed you that you were finished with your evidence but we have now had to call you back to complete one part of the evidence which the Prosecution wishes to deal with, according to the ruling of the Appeals Chamber. So the Prosecution can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I'll be not very long with you this morning and I've only got one small area that I need to cover with you. Before I get to the actual substance of the issue. Just let me remind you of what you said on this topic on the last occasion you were here in April. You were being asked questions by Mr. Pisarevic about the telephone call that you received to get you to go to the radio station and get it functioning, and this is very soon after the 17th. In fact it's on the 18th. You said this: Page 18618, "On the 18th of July, I got a phone call around 12.00, between 12.00 and 1300 hours. I heard the voice tell me, this is the Crisis Staff. You have a mission and you must carry out an order of the Crisis Staff. You have to make sure that the radio Bosanski Samac becomes operational. I then proceeded to ask a few questions but I was not given the permission to ask these questions. They told me I must carry out my task, I should not ask any questions, but I nevertheless wanted to know who was on the other side of the line and who had ordered that, who is the representative of the Crisis Staff on the telephone. And I was told, you know who is the President of the Crisis Staff, and the Crisis Staff ordered the following. And it was the President of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Blagoje Simic." That was from questioning by Mr. Pisarevic. You recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I then cross-examined you, page 18644. Question: "First of all on the 18th of April, Dr. Blagoje Simic called you and instructed you to get the radio station up and operating, am I correct?" Answer: "No. Stevan Todorovic was the one who gave me the instructions, according to the orders of Blagoje Simic." And then very shortly thereafter, at page 18645, I asked you this: "I'm only interested in the telephone call. It was the voice of Dr. Blagoje Simic and he was on the other end of the telephone. And he gave you the instructions to get the radio station up and running." Answer: "At the beginning of my testimony, I already said that a voice called from the Crisis Staff, that person did not introduce himself and even when I asked him who it was, he didn't want to tell me who it was, but he said that Dr. Blagoje Simic, the President of the Crisis Staff, ordered that the radio station should be up and operational." You recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And then I asked you this question, also at page 18645. "Have you ever told anyone, particularly towards the end of last year, meaning 2002, that it was Dr. Blagoje Simic who telephoned you and told you that the radio had to be put back in order and start broadcasting programmes? Have you ever told anyone that?" Answer: "I don't remember having ever told that to anyone but I said that through an intermediary, through a person, he had ordered that radio station should be put back in order." Do you remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So you don't recall ever having told anyone towards the end of last year that it was Dr. Blagoje Simic who telephoned you and told you that the radio had to be put back in order and start broadcasting programmes and so I would like to refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown his 92 bis statement, please, the unredacted version?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Antic I would like you please to look at your statement that you have placed in front of you, and you will find on the -- I believe the third page, your attestation that the statement is true and correct and your signature. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And of course at the time that you provided that statement to the officer of the Registry, you were endeavouring, weren't you, to be as accurate and as truthful as you could be?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at paragraph 15 of the statement. First sentence, and please read it out.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: "I think it was on the 18th of April, I was called on the phone by Blagoje Simic, who was the President of the Crisis Staff, and he said that the radio had to be put in order and that we had to start broadcasting programmes."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a matter of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, in B/C/S, [B/C/S spoken] which could be translated in various ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's just that objection. Maybe the interpreters could give us couple of versions how can -- how this can be translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the Trial Chamber has got official translation services and the interpreters are persons who have been properly appointed by the Tribunal. So the Trial Chamber is bound by their version of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if it's of any comfort to the Trial Chamber the answer that's interpreted is almost identical to that which is contained in paragraph 15 as translated. Furthermore, I can assure the Trial Chamber that I've been to no less than 3 interpreters and translators to check that very first sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has no problem with the interpretation received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, yes, I accept that and I just wanted to emphasise that point, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Antic, it's clear, in paragraph 15, that you said that you were telephoned by Blagoje Simic. Having seen that, having refreshed your memory as to what you said last year, is it your position now that you were telephoned in fact by Mr. Blagoje Simic who instructed you to get the radio station up and running?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: It's stated quite clearly here. I think it was on the 18th of April I was phoned by Blagoje Simic. This does not mean that I was personally called by Blagoje Simic, by Blagoje Simic himself. Perhaps it hasn't been put very well, but it really wasn't Blagoje Simic in person. We are talking about Stevan Todorovic and Simeon Simic. They then told me at that point that Blagoje Simic had ordered that the radio should start functioning. I never said that I was called by him on that day. Later, if I may explain, I phoned the Crisis Staff when I couldn't find anyone in the radio, when I couldn't find any of the six journalists, technicians, there, I phoned the Crisis Staff and Simic, Blagoje Simic, answered personally. Then he said that everything had to be done with regard to the radio. I had to phone Simeon Simic and Stevan Todorovic. I don't know how else to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with plea for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any Defence counsel wish to ask questions? I see none. Thank you very much, Mr. Antic, we are now through finally with you. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I just want to find out from you that whether or not you have now formally closed the case for the Defence of Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, actually I have some evidences to -- I mean, it's like evidentiary matters, housekeeping matters, that we have to -- I spoke with my friends from Prosecution regarding the ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you have some documents to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To explain, to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: A couple of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Thank you. First of all, Your Honour, the Defence was provided with the (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours? I apologise, I'm hiding at the back here. Can we move into private session for a moment, here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In regard to what Mr. Pantelic is saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think from way back since we moved from the first document discussed by Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can continue, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. So I will briefly repeat, so immediately after the Christmas break in our proceedings, intention of the Defence was to call Professor Aleksic, handwritten expert in Defence case, and then my learned friend, Mr. Weiner, indicated on page 13734 that there is a possibility that the Prosecution will not cross-examine this expert witness, and then he confirmed me during the break, and due to the fact that we were in some hurry with the Defence witnesses, formally I didn't tender this report into evidence, although he was filed through the fax so formally I'd like now to have a number for this report. And Madam Registrar informed me that copies are available for the Bench and for the other members in proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have a number? It wasn't even marked for identification, was it? No. There is no record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have a number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D184/1 and ter for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then, Your Honour, we discussed this particular evidentiary matters with our learned friends from the Prosecution, since on the list of Dr. Simic exhibits, there are a number of ID documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I think I can assist you and Mr. Pantelic and we can speed this up because I can quickly indicate what's not objected to and get this matter moving. Mr. Weiner also has some exhibits. They are not in order so from that point of view it might be a bit of a problem but other than that I can give you swift information. D20/1, no problems as far as the Prosecution is concerned. Do you want me to keep proceeding or shall we do them individually?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I think you proceed because they all have their own numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. D48/1. There is no problem. D70 -- the only other one of the Blagoje Simic exhibits that might cause a slight problem is D15/1. The Prosecution doesn't strenuously object but we can't see -- can't see its relevance. It's a document that deals with -- dated the 28th of May, an order to the command of the 102nd Odzak Brigade saying that 102 Brigade of the Odzak HVO has to coordinate the tending of cattle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a matter of weight, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's a matter of weight but the Prosecution cannot conceivably see its relevance. Other than that we have nothing to say on that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner has some, as well, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, we have -- good morning, Your Honours. We have no objections to D6/1, D7/1, D10/1, and D179/1. We have questions as to the basic relevance of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you go to that, to the ones where you have something to say, can we just have a formal record that these exhibits -- these documents will retain the same numbers as exhibits? I just want to make sure the Registry's records are correct. This is D6, D7, D10, D15, D20, D48, and D179, all of them /1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As long as the Registry receives the translations of a couple of documents, these will retain the same number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which ones don't have translations so that the record is corrected?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: At the moment I was able to find D15/1 and D20/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic? The English versions of D15 and D20, both of them /1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D70 which was mentioned /1 has already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I be corrected because on my document, I had D7. Is it D70?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: D7, not 70, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. It's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I think maybe the confusion was Mr. Di Fazio before you introduced the remaining documents, you were referring to, you actually said D70 and then went on to say something else so I think that's why D70 appeared on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That may be right because one of the -- one of Mr. Tadic's exhibits is a 70 exhibit, so that is probably right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Mr. Pantelic, we have the English versions or maybe you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have that, in fact, let me first address Trial Chamber with regard to Exhibit D15/1 ID. Just to shortly have -- have short reply on the position of the Prosecution. Well, in fact, the relevance, the Defence see the relevance with this particular document, because the -- in stamp of this particular document, and it is absolutely clear from the evidence D15/1 ter, that the HVO unit, 104, operated under the control of Republic of Croatia operational group east -- eastern Posavina, from -- with the seat in Slavonski Brod. Although it is not in dispute in this case that the certain military operations on the large scale from Croatian side conducted in Posavina region, still this is some kind of, one of the corroborative evidences which support Defence case with regard to the context of the conflict in Posavina region, and particular position of Samac municipality within that region, and it is also related with the creation of Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina and also it's related with the number of evidences that Croatian troops, with in assistance with the HVO units, practically took control over the, let's say, 95 per cent of Posavina region. And it is important for our case because our position is that Samac municipality was included in this plan and also that Samac was surrounded of enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then with regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So are you going to hand in the English versions to the Registry?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, in the exhibits we have official English translation of that particular document, D15/1, but there is no stamp, which can be -- if I may suggest, which can be very easily we can overcome that problem because it's in Latinic script on the exhibit D15/1 and it's just readable that it's republic of Croatia and operational group so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe that to be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then the other one, D20, I think where the Registry says they haven't got the English version yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. With regard -- yes. With regard to Exhibit D20/1, I will take immediate steps to obtain official translation and during next couple of days, I will tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because there is no problem. It's already an exhibit, only that we must have the English translation. Yes. Can you move on to the other documents, if any?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you. Now I would like to give the basis for the admission of Defence Exhibit D2/1 ID. First of all, I have sufficient number of copies of translation of that document, because according to notes here in the list of exhibits, we at that time, during the cross-examination of Dr. Donia, we operated with an unofficial translation so I kindly ask Ms. Usher to take these five copies of this particular document and to provide it to the Bench. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the position of the OTP? Because the notes show you wanted to check --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There was no authentication of the document at the time, and also there is a serious issue to relevance here. But it's -- I mean, it's not a strong objection. We don't see how it's relevant. I'll even get beyond the position of authentication, I don't see how it's relevant, once again, if he can explain how it's relevant, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But you have no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: For whatever value it's worth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a matter of weight, isn't it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will explain, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we can have it admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can explain, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour, it's quite important document for us since it covers the activity -- just in few words, activity and directions of the main headquarters of SDS [sic] party with regard to the movement of population, of Muslim population, in area of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also there is a -- some mentions regarding the -- you see at the first moment that -- the first paragraph, they are speaking about this security situation in Bosnia and then that Karadzic and his clique in Pale adopted Geneva documents and basically this is an instruction of the SDA headquarters of movement of Muslim population, a suggestion to leave, and this is a core of our case, so in general context, we shall use this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Just a small point, page 18, line 3, you apparently intended to say SDA instead of SDS. The main headquarters of -- it reads the main headquarters of SDS party. You mean SDA party?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was obviously a slip of the tongue or maybe a mistake in the reporting. I'm grateful for your intervention, of course it's SDA because document speaks for itself. And also, Your Honour, allow me to -- with the same regard, and regarding the previous document, D20/1, I've been just informed, my colleague, Mr. Vukovic, that we actually have official translation, so I kindly ask Ms. Usher to assist me. This is also the SDA document from Sarajevo regarding their actions and there is some relevance to this particular document. Yes, Your Honour, and one last issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour, in terms of procedural issues, I was at the conference with the commanding officer of UNDU, Mr. McFadden, and I mean in official capacity to ask and to request the report of detention unit with regard to my client, Dr. Simic, which is the usual practice in our proceedings, and I was advised that according to the practice, I have to raise that to -- before Trial Chamber and then officially through the Registry, UNDU will file this particular report of the -- of behaviour of Dr. Simic during the period of his detention within the unit, within the UNDU. So just for the record, or -- I believe that the Registry will take necessary steps for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It is the wish of your client to have this formal report placed on record?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, yes. This is actually our common position in order to have an overall view of the case, and also for mitigating sent -- mitigating circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I have the attention of the Registry assistant, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. The Trial Chamber will request the Registry to ask the detention unit to formally file a report on Dr. Blagoje Simic during the period of his detention, which will form part of his Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just two minor issues. I was just informed by the Registrar. It is the Exhibit D178/1, ID. Actually that was the extract of the book which I tendered on 8th of April, 2003. It's a part of the book of Colonel Stublincevic, at that time he was a commander of 17th Corps operating in the area of Samac, and actually that was the relevance for this document -- to this document, and I just would like to find out whether Mr. Re has some objections to that. So could we have full number for this particular evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The -- what is the position of the Prosecution? This is D178/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It speaks of the plan of JNA in this region and the role of 17 Corps of JNA in operations, simply as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution says it appears to be an extract from a book, from a person whose qualifications to give the account are unknown. We simply ask the Defence to inform the Trial Chamber of how it is relevant to the Defence of Dr. Simic. If Mr. Pantelic can do that, the Prosecution won't object. But on the face of it, it's pretty marginal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Gladly. The author of this book is Colonel Stublincevic, he was a commander of 17 Corps of JNA, which was superior unit of 17th Tactical Group, and it is corroborative evidence from Defence point of view to the certain relevance of the document -- of reports by JNA, and these are the exhibits P19, 20, 21, 22, 23, actually reporting of the war -- military operations in that area. And it is -- the importance for the Defence of Dr. Simic is that we have our position that, first, Dr. Simic was any -- in any capacity participant of all this operations and it's with direct relation with the -- with his alleged participation in subcharge 1 of Count 1, forcible takeover. So all these military issues are important for the Defence of Dr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There you are, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution's response is we won't object but it has almost no weight. There is an account at page 526 of the English version relating to the 16th and 17th of April, 1992, in the Svilaja, Brusnica, Bosanski Samac, Odzak and Modrica, of clashes between the Croatian and Serb forces. The Prosecution simply notes that this is evidence which is in dispute in the case. The author of the book is not here and is not subject to cross-examination as to the truth of clashes between the two forces on the 16th and 17th of April. That's all. But with that caveat, the Prosecution doesn't object to the document going in for what it's worth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Yes, any other documents, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we could have actually -- so we have a number for this particular evidence? The ID will be removed? Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it will retain the same number as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the other evidence is D181/1 ter ID. During the examination of witness of Mr. Zaric, Colonel Nikolic, commander of 17th Tactical Group, during the cross-examination, I tendered -- well, actually, I confronted the witness with this particular document, actually the content of this document. It's very simple document. It's a number of telephone, and nickname, number of telephone was actually the telephone of Colonel Nikolic when he was deployed back in Serbia, and he confirmed his nickname, Kriger, which is on this particular piece of paper. Well obviously, reason -- I mean the basis for the relevance for the defence of Dr. Simic is that this particular document, defence received from our learned friends, from Prosecution side, and this particular document is a part of personal belongings and personal archives so to say of Slobodan Miljkovic, aka Lugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what is the relevance to your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The relevance is that even after the period of -- when Colonel Nikolic withdrew from Bosnia, since the number is of his military unit in Serbia, the telephone number, the only conclusion that we can make is that he still at that time, after 19th of May, 1992, he was in contact with Lugar, which is the other part of relevance for defence of Dr. Simic is that although we have enough evidences, that paramilitary units actually volunteers, were under the control of Colonel Nikolic and 17th Tactical Group, and in addition, obviously certain level of relation still were between Colonel Nikolic and Lugar, even after 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the position of the Prosecution on this one? Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Pantelic -- my recollection of Mr. Nikolic's evidence was he said he didn't remember if that was his telephone number. Can Mr. Pantelic assist with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we checked our documents, we established that three documents that were offered by the Defence of Miroslav Tadic as exhibits had an ID marking. utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a document D74/3. utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just one matter, if Your Honours please. You recall during the evidence of Dr. Radovanovic, I put to her two maps that I had obtained from the web site of the IMG group. The Defence, in fact Mr. Pantelic, pointed out that their researchers had indicated that it was the world's largest, most diverse and only truly global company dedicated to the marketing and management of sport, leisure and life-style goods. The front page of the web site indicates that the international management group was established in 1993 as a specialised intergovernmental agency in accordance with UN resolution 179 dated November 21, 1947. Its operations relate and I quote here, "to the accountability of the IMG steering committee formed of the members representing the European Commission, something called ECO, Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey and the United Kingdom. Additional support members are OHR, the Office of the High Representative of Bosnia, and UNHCR, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees." And the -- and it continues. It's essentially involved in reconstruction efforts in Bosnia. And that's where the maps were obtained from. I don't -- I provided copies of this web site to -- the front page of the web site to Defence counsel. If Your Honours please, the purpose of putting those two maps to Dr. Radovanovic was simply to place them in front of her and ask her if it altered her conclusions, not to prove that the four municipalities that emerged out of the basic territory of the former two municipalities were polarised. In order to do that we rely on the evidence of Dr. Tabeau and her reports. So that was the only purpose of putting those two maps to Dr. Radovanovic, to see, in effect, if it altered her opinion. They remain as exhibits P184 ID and P184A ID, and the Prosecution seeks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: My record shows P183. Can we hear from the Registry assistant?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The two colourful maps are P183 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, there must be a mistake in my transcript. I accept what the Registry says. I'm referring to the two colourful maps. If it's P183 and P183A ID then they are the ones I'm referring to and I'm seeking the tender into evidence of those two maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the position of the Defence with the explanation that the Prosecution has given now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence objects to these two maps being admitted into evidence because these maps do not explain the purpose for which the maps were drafted and based on what documentation it was done. Based on the submission of the Prosecution, it doesn't follow that this organisation is engaged in any demographic research. It seems more that they are dealing with urban issues, energy, transport, telecommunications management and so on which is quite unrelated to demographic research and assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm informed that Mr. Di Fazio wanted to reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just to say this if Your Honours please, Mr. Krgovic pointed out precisely what I was pointing out to you. I'm not using them to prove the polarisation in the former municipalities. I will rely on the evidence of Dr. Tabeau and her report to do that. It was put to her to see if she would alter her opinion in the light of what they claim. That's all. So there is no need to analyse the source and the origins and how the maps were produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will have them admitted into evidence. It is a matter of how much weight to be attached to them. So they will retain the same numbers. Any other matters?

utterances.text: Yes. Can we move into private session?

utterances.text: Yes, can we have the numbers formally, please? Yes, we are in open session now. We are in open session. Yeah.

utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D183A/1, B and C, thank you.

utterances.text: Thank you. This will follow the order in which they were numbered by Mr. Pantelic. Any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. There is two other matters. The first one is the Prosecution just wishes to seek some brief clarification in relation to the Trial Chamber's ruling of the acceptance into evidence of P164, that is the factual basis for the plea of guilty in the case of Biljana Plavsic. The Prosecution -- the brief history is the Prosecution was examined, cross-examining, a witness, Mr. Makso Simeunovic on the 3rd of March, 2003, and asked that the plea agreement or the factual basis be marked for identification and the Trial Chamber asked whether we wished to have it admitted into evidence and it was admitted into evidence. On the 8th of April, the Defence led by Mr. Pantelic for Dr. Simic asked for access to certain documents relating to or about -- behind the factual basis for the plea of guilty and two days later, the Trial Chamber ruled that was on the 10th of April, saying that -- handing -- just saying, hand down a ruling regarding the oral motion by the Defence on the use of the guilty plea by Mrs. Plavsic. "The Trial Chamber is of the view that it does not require the documents sought by the Defence in their oral motion for them to challenge any evidence adduced by the Prosecution when using the guilty plea by Mrs. Plavsic. The Defence can examine their witnesses just as they do, can re-examine their witnesses just as they do with every other piece of evidence or exhibit produced by the Prosecution. The production of documents enumerated by the Defence in this regard is unnecessary as it is not our role to inquire into or evaluate the merits of the plea and the sentencing judgement." That's the extract of Your Honour's oral ruling in relation to the use of the Plavsic factual basis for the plea of guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution just wishes to clarify so it's completely clear for the Defence and the Trial Chamber when we were cross-examining witnesses and using that document, we were assuming that the Trial Chamber had admitted it under the basis of Rule 94(B) which is taking judicial notice of a document used in another case and the Prosecution was using the document only for the purposes of confronting witnesses in cross-examination to say, to put forward a version of events given by the leader of the SDS and the president of the -- Presidency of the Republika Srpska at the relevant time. And asking, confronting the witnesses with it and asking them whether or not they adopted -- would adopt that version or would change their own evidence in the light of that evidence. The Prosecution makes clear that it was only intending to make a limited use of that document from another case and that being only confrontation of witnesses in another case -- confrontation of witnesses in this case in relation to a document produced in another case, the same use, the Prosecution could make of any document or any version by or hearsay version of anyone outside this case and asking them whether or not in the light of that they agreed with it or were prepared to change their evidence. So we are putting on the record just to make it abundantly clear that that was the use the Prosecution was making. We just ask clarification from the Trial Chamber, is the Prosecution's assumption correct that, as it wasn't explicitly set out in the Trial Chamber's ruling, the Trial Chamber was admitting it only on the basis of Rule 94(B) and for that limited use because the Prosecution certainly won't be submitting anything else in its final Trial Chamber brief as to the use which it says the Trial Chamber can make of that factual basis for the plea of guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is the basis upon which the guilty plea was admitted and the Trial Chamber does not wish to say anything, that has been clarified, I think, sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The final matter which I wish to raise is -- I'm sorry, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Please, Your Honour, just for the record, Defence of Dr. Simic would like to submit respectfully submit the following: If this particular document, factual basis of plea agreement, is going to be considered as a document with -- on the basis of judicial notice from the other proceedings, then I think it would be appropriate to remove this particular exhibit from the list of exhibits. These are the submissions which are absolutely based. Then to have -- because it's a public document, it's within the jurisdiction and the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, so in that case, I think this document cannot be officially on the list of exhibits, because my understanding was that he was a recognised through the procedure of judicial notice as a document from the other proceedings. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, Mr. Pantelic. Any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour doesn't wish me to respond to Mr. Pantelic's submission in relation to it remaining as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm wondering whether there is anything else to say, unless you have something extra apart from what you already submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's just Mr. Pantelic raised something else. He said it should be removed and if Your Honours are considering removing it I would like to be heard but if Your Honours aren't I won't say anything.

utterances.text: No we are not considering removing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please the Court, may it please Your Honours. The final matter which I wish to raise is in relation to the final trial brief and the format of it or the content of it. The Trial Chamber has heard a lot of evidence which has either been in closed session or in private session and the reasons for it being heard in private or closed session is obviously so as not to reveal the identity of a witness through information which is given by the -- by a witness or other people in court which relates to them. However, there is a lot of information given in private session which, if carefully or if properly used, will not reveal the identity of any -- of any protected witness or the identity of anyone whose identity should not be disclosed. The Prosecution will of course file a public -- sorry, a confidential version of its final trial brief which of course will refer in full to the witnesses who gave evidence in closed session and any evidence which has to remain out of the public domain at the moment and of course will then will file a publicly redacted version. The Prosecution seeks guidance in this manner. What we would like to do, if possible, is to refer to some evidence in closed session in the publicly redacted version in such a way as to -- as it could not identify the -- could not identify the protected witness or someone whose identity has been protected by the Trial Chamber. Obviously we would do it very, very carefully but balancing of course the public interest in having as much information on the public record as possible with the protection of the -- of the witnesses, what we would like to do if possible is to refer to some evidence which is given in closed session but evidence which doesn't identify someone because often there is a lot of stuff which just won't identify anyone but which is evidence which would like to refer to. That's the first part of that. The second part is the brief is due on the 19th of June and the Prosecution will certainly have its confidential brief filed on that date. However, it will take us several days to properly redact everything from it because we can't file a public version because we can't do two at the same time. We can only file a publicly redacted version after we have finished and signed off on the confidential version because we have to then go through it extremely carefully and take everything out. While we are drafting it, we've blocked everything we think is in closed session or highlighted it so that we can take it out but we can't really have two running versions at the same time because versions get lost and it becomes a nightmare to try and control two versions when you're altering them as you go. What we had like to ask the Trial Chamber in relation to that is can we file the publicly redacted version say on the Monday after we filed the confidential version on the Thursday which would give us time to make sure that there was nothing in the public version that should not be there. Of course there would no prejudice to the other side who will have the confidential version on the Thursday and of course to the Trial Chamber which would have the full version before the weekend. So those are the two matters I raise or seek guidance in relation to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber agrees with that, as long as the confidential one, which is fully dealing with the whole case, is filed on the due date, on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else from the Defence?

utterances.text: Is Your Honour saying that you also agree with the first proposal which is to put in the publicly redacted version matters from private session which couldn't identify a witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, generally that is the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the protection really is the identification of the witness. So if that is done carefully by the Prosecution, there should not be any problem. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I was just advised by the Registry that actually there is one more document on our list that still has an ID mark. It's document D50/4 ter ID.
